title: Isolate — Sub-Agents & Clean Windows
subtitle: Split the mess into a clean window, return only the conclusion — and pay isolation's honest price on single questions
topics: The isolate strategy — a sub-agent's exploration stays in its own window
The condensed hand-back — 1–2K-token summaries, not transcripts
Isolation's price — MedFlow's isolated mode costs MORE than naive on single questions
When the price inverts — long sessions and parallel exploration
Task-context alignment — compaction vs notes vs sub-agents, the full table

analogy.title: Sending a Junior to the Archives
analogy.text: A partner preparing for trial doesn't read forty boxes of discovery herself — she sends a junior associate, whose desk gets buried in folders, sticky notes, and dead ends. What comes back to the partner is a two-page memo. The mess stayed in the archive room; only the conclusion crossed the threshold. But notice the economics: for ONE quick question, sending the junior costs more than looking it up yourself — the briefing, the walk, the memo-writing. The junior pays off when the digging is deep, parallel, or would trash the partner's own desk for the rest of the week.

antiPatterns: Isolation as a reflex — spawning a sub-agent for a one-line lookup pays the briefing tax for nothing; MedFlow's isolated mode is the most expensive receipt on the board for exactly this reason (median 1,805 vs naive 1,696, replay grid)
Transcript hand-backs — a sub-agent that returns its whole exploration re-imports the mess isolation existed to contain
Unbriefed juniors — a sub-agent with a vague charter explores everything and concludes nothing; the hand-back contract (scope + summary budget) IS the technique

sections.title: The Fourth Strategy: Split It
sections.body:
Isolate is the last of the four canonical strategies [LC-WSCI]: 'give a sub-agent its own clean window, let it do the messy work, and return only the conclusion to the parent.' Anthropic's architecture guidance is concrete: specialized sub-agents 'handle focused tasks with clean context windows, returning condensed summaries of 1,000–2,000 tokens' to the coordinator [ANTHROPIC-CE].

MedFlow's isolated mode implements the honest version: a second model call receives a minimal, clean context for the data-gathering subtask, and its ≤1,500-token summary — not its working — feeds the main answer. The sub-call's tokens land in the tool layer of the receipt, because isolation's price should be visible, not hidden in another window.

sections.title: The Honest Receipt: Isolation Costs More Here
sections.body:
Read the grid without flinching: isolated's median is 1,805 tokens — MORE than naive's 1,696 — and it is the most expensive mode on every single standing question (replay grid, synthetic-pre-recording). Q9: isolated 1,796 vs notes 167. The reason is structural: our standing questions are single-shot, and a single-shot task pays the sub-agent's full briefing + exploration + summary on top of the main call, while amortizing it over exactly one answer.

This is not a failed mode — it is the course's clearest demonstration that strategies have task shapes. A benchmark of one-question sessions is precisely the shape isolation is worst at. Publishing this number anyway, labeled, is the Honesty Rule doing its job: the same rule that voided compressed's Q9 'saving' protects isolated's honest loss from being hidden.

sections.title: Where Isolation Wins
sections.body:
Invert the shape and the price inverts. Long sessions: the sub-agent's exploration never enters the parent window, so it never compounds — the parent's later calls don't re-carry it, while naive re-pays its dumps on every turn (U08's climbing sparkline). Parallel exploration: three sub-agents reading three members' histories concurrently return three memos; the parent pays 3×~1,500 instead of 3× full transcripts forever after. Contamination control: a sub-agent that waded through irrelevant records can't pollute the parent's attention budget — the parent only ever saw the memo.

The parent KG course measured the same pattern at repo scale (M12: a subagent's 40 file reads stay in its context; the main conversation gets a 200-word summary). The kit's M26 quantifies the sharing-pattern costs. The rule of thumb: isolate when the exploration is bigger than the conclusion — and will be referenced again.

sections.title: The Alignment Table, Complete
sections.body:
Track 3 closes with Anthropic's full task-context alignment [ANTHROPIC-CE]: compaction for extensive back-and-forth needing conversational continuity; note-taking for iterative work with identifiable milestones; sub-agents for complex exploration that benefits from parallelism or would trash the parent's window. These are not competing brands — they are answers to different task shapes, and U12 will turn this table plus the measured grid into a router.

The receipts you've now read make the table concrete: compaction's saw-tooth, notes' flat 198, isolation's expensive-now-cheap-later. Choosing among them from evidence rather than fashion is the competency this track built.

sections.title: The Hand-Back Contract
sections.code:
# Isolation lives or dies by the hand-back contract: bounded scope in,
# bounded summary out. (Numbers cited: bench/results/fullgrid-compact.csv.)

SUMMARY_BUDGET_TOKENS = 1500

def isolated_subtask(charter: str, records: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Simulates the sub-agent call: messy exploration stays in HERE."""
    # ... imagine 40 records read, dead ends, re-reads: none of it escapes ...
    relevant = [r for r in records if r["member"] == "M-2001"]
    summary = ("MEMO re " + charter + ":\n" +
               "\n".join(f"  {r['id']}: {r['decision']} (score {r['score']})"
                          for r in relevant) +
               "\n  No eligibility denials on file for this member.")
    # the contract, enforced: a memo, never a transcript
    assert len(summary) // 4 <= SUMMARY_BUDGET_TOKENS, "hand-back over budget"
    return summary

def parent_ask(question: str, records: list[dict]) -> str:
    memo = isolated_subtask("M-2001 authorization history", records)
    # parent context = question + memo. The archive room stays behind.
    parent_context = f"{memo}\n\nQUESTION: {question}"
    print(f"parent carries {len(parent_context)//4} tokens - not the exploration")
    return parent_context

records = [
    {"id": "PA-1001", "member": "M-2001", "decision": "APPROVED", "score": 100},
    {"id": "PA-1004", "member": "M-2001", "decision": "MANUAL_REVIEW", "score": 65},
    {"id": "PA-1003", "member": "M-2005", "decision": "DENIED", "score": 25},
]
parent_ask("Summarize M-2001's history", records)
# One question: this costs MORE than just answering (isolated 1,796 vs
# notes 167 on Q9). Ten follow-ups that reuse the memo: the price inverts.
# The contract is what makes either arithmetic possible.

sections.question: MedFlow's isolated mode is the most expensive mode on every standing question. WHY does the course ship that number instead of tuning the benchmark until isolation wins?
options: A. An oversight — the benchmark should be fixed

B. Because the grid measures single-shot questions — isolation's worst shape — and publishing the labeled loss teaches task-context alignment; hiding it would be the same sin as celebrating compressed's voided Q9 saving
D. Because sub-agents only work with larger models
sections.explanation: Honesty Rule: numbers state their conditions. Isolated 1,805 median vs naive 1,696 on one-shot questions is TRUE and shape-dependent — the same mode wins long parallel sessions where exploration would otherwise compound. A benchmark that only shows wins is marketing.

sections.question: WHEN is spawning a sub-agent the right call for a MedFlow reviewer's request?
options: A. Always — clean windows are always better

B. For 'check whether any of our 6 members has inconsistent determinations across their full history' — deep parallel exploration whose conclusion is small and reusable — not for 'what's PA-1002's score?'
C. Whenever the question mentions more than one entity
D. Only when the main window is completely full
sections.explanation: Isolate when exploration >> conclusion and the conclusion will be reused. The audit sweep buries a desk (perfect junior work, parallelizable per member); the score lookup is one record — paying briefing+memo tax for it is the anti-pattern the 1,805 median prices.

sections.title: What Goes Wrong
items: Sub-agent theater — 'multi-agent' architectures where every agent shares one transcript anyway; that's naive mode with extra steps and extra cost (the kit's M26 hub-vs-blackboard token math)
Recursive delegation — sub-agents spawning sub-agents until the summaries' summaries lose the load-bearing facts; depth needs the same fidelity discipline as compression
Hidden accounting — folding sub-call tokens into nowhere so isolation looks free; MedFlow bills them to the tool layer so the receipt tells the whole truth

takeaway: Isolation moves the mess to a clean window and returns only the conclusion — a tax on single questions, a bargain on deep parallel work — and the receipt should always show the tax.
labUnderstand: Compare Q9 receipts in isolated (1,796 — tool layer carries the sub-call) vs notes (167) and naive (1,700), then reason about the 10-follow-up session where isolation's memo amortizes. You compute the break-even turn count yourself.
labBuild: With Claude writing the code, build handback_contract.py: an isolated subtask with an enforced memo budget, then a 12-turn simulated session comparing cumulative cost of naive re-carry vs memo reuse. Break it on purpose by returning the transcript instead of the memo and watch the contract assertion refuse the hand-back.
